answers.core: I am unaware of any methods to manipulate `@export` notation outside of modifying Godot's source code.
answers.workaround:
It's possible to work around it by storing the exported variable as 100 times the preferred value, adding the argument `"suffix:%"`, and dividing it by 100 when it should be used. This changes a simple `damage * damage_modifier` to `damage * damage_modifier / 100`.

This is similar to what you might do if the `"radians"` argument did not exist. You would have to store the value in degrees and use `deg_to_rad` whenever you'd like to use it. For example, you'd have to type `Vector2.RIGHT.rotated(deg_to_rad(angle))`.

Ultimately, it's much easier to intuitively convert between numbers and percentages than it is to convert between radians and degrees. `"radians"` is closer to quality-of-life, while `"percent"` would be closer to syntactic sugar. I believe percentages are a common enough unit to be worth adding anyway; any more and I would honestly just suggest adding some sort of "display multiplier" field to replace all of them. (Perhaps that should be a separate proposal?)
